decisions.reason: The report traces DSH-0.1.2-A1-02 (alpha.1 temporarily removed SessionEvent.ignorable) and DSH-0.1.2-A2-01 (alpha.2 restored retention semantics), computes the remove-then-restore corridor net state, and applies the final alpha.2 state to produceExternalEvent in src/events.ts, concluding the defense must be deleted. Version history is correct and grounded in the sealed cards, not just card names.

The report locates the delete (event as any).ignorable statement, explicitly rejects the comment's instruction to keep the defense, and recommends deleting the stripping line and correcting the obsolete rationale. It notes the shown literal never sets ignorable so the delete is effectively a no-op, while still rejecting the stripping policy, and it distinguishes removing the stripping code from removing the marker itself.

The report explains producers should set ignorable:true only for informational events whose semantics old readers can omit without breaking reconstruction, that the marker is not a consumer-side filtering directive and marked events remain in the loaded log after reload, and it applies this to the third-party/informational producer while respecting the live Session.append limitation.

The report identifies the capability gap that public live Session.append has no ignorable parameter, forbids faking the entry via a cast or unsupported argument (recommends filing the gap upstream instead), and defers the exact producer/persistence integration rather than inventing an API, flagging unverified declaration details as unconfirmed per the closed-book brief.

caps.reason: The final recommendation affirmatively deletes the alpha.1 defense on alpha.2 and explains why keeping it is harmful; the old stripping code is quoted only for diagnosis and rejected, so the cap's condition is not met.
